text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania is serious candidate for location of SHARP plant, SHARP executive manager for Europe said when SHARROM, distributor of SHARP products in Balkan country opened.
- Eleven companies applied for listing on Bucharest stock exchange, which will also handle public share offers for 14 state-run companies.
- Private bank Banca Romaneasca SA has launched electronic transfer system for individuals.
- State-owned bank Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA gives hard currency loans for machinery imports.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's first nuclear reactor has become fully operational.
- Romanian agriculture got only 43 percent of disel fuel needed for farming works last month.
ADEVARUL
- Farming sectors in Romania and Bulgaria lag behind other countries bidding for EU integration.
- Bucharest city hall suggested pensioners living on pensions below 250,000 lei a month should benefit from free urban transport starting mid-October.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Some 800,000 tonnes of crude oil are expected in Black Sea port of Constanta in October.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Price of fuel will rise by 25 percent starting January 1997, when special road fund becomes effective.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- National Unity Party (PUNR) leader, Gheorghe Funar, bears political responsability for Caritas money spinning scheme which collapsed in 1994 after sucking in $1.0 billion worth of savings from millions of Romanians, said President Ion Iliescu.
- Two-page report on state television allegedly serving the interests of present government.
- George Padure, mayor of Bucharest's first district -- the capital's main residential area -- resignes three months after local elections.
ADEVARUL
- Newspaper presents all 16 presidential candidates registered with the Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) for the November 3 polls.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- People contacted during fake poll commissioned by the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) should file complaints with prosecution, says sociologists Dan Baciu.
- Scandal of phone polls is "minor issue", said President Iliescu.
- Retired General Nicolae Militaru, Romania's first post-communist Defence Minister, runs as independent candidate in presidential race.
- PDSR is responsible for collapse of Caritas scheme, as many members of government, presidency and PDSR allegedly had got "bags of money" from the scheme, said Funar.
ZIUA
- Newspaper says electoral campaign of ruling PDSR to cost 1,500 billion lei ($460 million).
- Poll commissioned by ruling PDSR is unprofessional, a mascarde made only to launch rumours among voters, say managers of various polling institutes.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Meteorologists say Romania expects harsh winter starting mid-November.
DIMINEATA
- Newspaper publishes excerpts from book titled "Moments of History" by President Iliescu on split of post-revolutionary National Salvation Front in 1992.
VREMEA
- Excerpts from Senate's report on December 1989 events. ($=3,261 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
